items.titleZh: 国际汽联远程操作中心升级至3.0版
items.summaryZh: 国际汽联本周正式启用远程操作中心（ROC）3.0版，该中心位于F1比金山总部，自夏休期以来已投入运行。

media.altZh: 国际汽联远程操作中心升级至3.0版 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: '3.0' - How F1's post-2021 race control aid has changed
items.summaryEn: The FIA officially launched version 3.0 of its Remote Operations Centre (ROC) this week, located at F1's Biggin Hill headquarters and in operation since the summer break.
detailZh: 2021年阿布扎比站的阴影或许永远不会完全消散，但当天犯下的错误暴露出国际汽联需要更好地运营F1比赛。
过多压力集中在单个人身上、现场赛事控制缺乏支持、系统不够先进以及员工需求不断扩大，意味着改变不仅是可取的，而且是必要的。
在那场争议性冠军决战的风波中上任的国际汽联主席穆罕默德·本·苏拉耶姆承诺采取直接行动，他批准的首批事项之一就是设立远程操作中心（ROC），以提供更多支持、建议和后备保障。
国际汽联于2022年初在日内瓦设立了首个ROC，但当时相当基础。本周ROC 3.0正式启用，本·苏拉耶姆和F1首席执行官斯特凡诺·多梅尼卡利出席。
如今，在国际汽联位于比金山的总部里，有一间专门辟出的房间，比赛周末约有14名分析师值守在里面的办公桌前，自夏休期以来一直在持续运作。
ROC是做什么的？
作为国际汽联（FIA）和F1管理公司（FOM）的联合举措，ROC是大奖赛顺利运行的四项关键组成部分之一，与赛事控制、系统运行和赛事干事协同工作。
它的工作覆盖面很广，例如判断赛车是否因超出赛道限制而违规、裁定潜在的黄旗违规行为、在起步时检查赛车是否停在自己的发车格内，以及监控各类事件以帮助赛事控制更好地评估是否需要出动安全车或出示红旗。
ROC 接收来自赛道的实时数据，包括 140 多路音视频信号、车辆定位遥测和无线电通信。系统还采用了先进技术，包括 AI 辅助形状识别、计算机视觉和无线电消息自动标记，以帮助标记赛道上的事故。
ROC 的核心优势之一是，可以利用技术和人工交互来分担赛事控制中心的任务，而赛事控制中心在赛道现场已经忙得不可开交。
赛道限制的判定方式就是一个完美的例子。系统采用三层自动化系统来判定——包括计算机视觉、赛车线偏差和地理围栏。
AI 会预先过滤掉大约 90% 的赛道限制违规，因为这些违规非常明显，因此人工只需详细评估剩下 10% 处于边缘情况的违规。
这将最大限度减少时间浪费，并确保对真正重要的边缘案例进行应有的尽职调查。
ROC 的角色不是在决定赛道限制处罚时充当法官、陪审团和行刑者；它的角色是提供所有信息，以便干事们能够自行做出判罚。
国际汽联体育总监蒂姆·马利昂表示：“最终是干事们删除圈速——因此他们会随后复核，以确保自己对此满意。”
“显然，在某些情况下这是一个快速的决定。在其他更接近边缘的情况下，则需要稍长一些时间。”
还有一个关键层面，ROC 在其中可以发挥重要作用，那就是决策过程的透明度。
因此，一旦做出删除某个圈速的判定，相关证据会立即发送给车队，向他们说明原因。
马利昂补充道：“我认为我们之所以能够较为成功地让赛道限制完全不再成为争议话题，原因之一就是我们部署了这项技术、共享了这项技术，并向所有车队自由分发证据。”
但 ROC 的作用不仅限于规则事务，它还在一些安全事项上为赛事控制提供支持。
从乔治·拉塞尔在2024年澳大利亚大奖赛倒数第二圈撞车事故中得到的一个教训是，赛事控制中心需要更好地了解撞车后赛车和车手的状态信息。
所以现在有了一个专门的工作台，可以帮助调出所有相关的车载画面和信息，以帮助赛事控制中心判断需要采取何种干预措施。
马利昂补充道：“当时我们意识到，我们需要一种更快的方式来识别出现问题的赛车，并提供关于那一辆赛车的所有信息，以便评估它所在的位置——它处于安全位置吗？它处于不安全位置吗？——并让我们能够尽快推进到必要的中和状态。”
自2022年以来，赛事控制中心的转变是巨大的，正如马利昂所说，它现在的位置与起步时已天差地别。但同样，时间对于真正理解需要什么至关重要。
“ROC 1.0 最初创立时只有四个人，有时多一两个人，”他说。“实际上，作为一套设施，我当时相当满意。它很快就成型了。
“我们得以重新利用一张旧赛事控制台——但它终究只是一间改造过的会议室，里面放着一张赛事控制台和一块小得多的视频墙。
“刚开始时，我们显然必须理解这项技术，但我们也必须理解各种关系和职责，而这件事是相当自然地逐步发展起来的。我们很幸运，那里有几位关键人物，他们曾在车队或类似环境中使用过类似设施，因而具备相关经验。
“因此，我想说，在头六个月里，能力提升非常、非常显著，信任也逐步建立起来。”
“我认为这确实是成功的关键，真正在赛事控制与赛事控制中心（ROC）之间建立信任，并理解正确的合作方式，从而成为有效的力量倍增器，而不仅仅是另一个声音。”
“而且有时候，如你所知，在时间压力下，一个明确做出决定的单一声音显然非常重要。”
归根结底，在监管执行方面，技术永远无法取代人类——但赛事控制中心（ROC）打算做的是降低犯错的风险。
正如本·苏拉耶姆所说：“尽量减少人为错误非常重要——但消除人为因素是不可能的。”
更充分的信息有助于做出更明智的决策，但ROC的价值还在于确保赛事控制中心和赛事总监能够专注于关键区域，而不会因为必须处理本可在别处解决的事务而不堪重负。
2021年阿布扎比事件的调查结论认为，把过多压力压在个人肩上只会增加犯错的风险。
如果ROC 3.0在2021年就已存在，那么当年的阿布扎比大奖赛可能不会演变成后来的样子。
但正如本·苏拉耶姆所说，时间无法倒流，重要的是已尽一切努力确保同样的错误不会在未来重演。
“这个承诺已经兑现了，”他说。“2021年在阿布扎比发生的事情本可以避免。但我们无法回到过去。我们必须面向未来。”
detailEn: While the ghosts of Abu Dhabi 2021 may never vanish totally, errors made that day exposed how the FIA needed to run Formula 1 races better.

Too much pressure placed on single individuals, a lack of support for race control on site, not advanced enough systems and the ever-expanding demands on staff meant change was not just desirable but essential.

Arriving amid the fallout of that controversial title decider, FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem promised direct action, and one of the first things he greenlit was a Remote Operations Centre (ROC) to offer more support, advice and back-up.
The FIA set up its first ROC in Geneva in early 2022, but it was quite a basic affair. This week ROC 3.0 was officially launched – with Ben Sulayem and F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali in attendance.
Now in a bespoke room at F1’s Biggin Hill headquarters, filled with desks that are manned by around 14 analysts on race weekends, it has been working away since the summer break.
What does ROC do?
As a joint initiative of the FIA and FOM, ROC is one of four key components for the smooth running of grands prix – working alongside race control, systems operations, and the stewards.

It covers a lot of ground – such as whether cars are in or out for track limit offences, judging potential yellow flag infringements, checking if cars are in their grid slots at the start, and monitoring incidents to help race control better evaluate if safety car or red flag responses are needed.

Feeding into ROC is live data from the track, including more than 140 audio and video feeds, car positioning telemetry and radio communications. Advanced technology is also used, including AI-assisted shape recognition, computer vision and automatic radio message tagging to help flag on-track incidents.
One of ROC’s core benefits is that technology and human interaction can be used to take tasks away from a race control that has its hands full at the track.
How track limits are judged is a perfect example. A three-layer automated system is used to work things out – comprising computer vision, racing-line deviation and geofencing.
AI will pre-filter roughly 90% of track limit breaches because they are so obvious, so a human only needs to assess in detail the 10% that are marginal.
This minimises time-wasting and ensures that proper diligence is done on the borderline ones that matter.
ROC’s role is not to be judge, jury and executioner in deciding on track limits penalties; it is to provide all the information so the stewards can make the calls themselves.
Tim Malyon, the FIA’s sporting director, said: “Ultimately it's the stewards that delete a lap - so they will then review just to make sure that they're happy.
“Obviously in some cases it's a quick decision. In other cases where it's a bit more borderline, it takes a bit longer.”
There is another critical layer where ROC has an important role to play, and that is transparency of the decision-making processes.
So once a call has been made to delete a laptime, the relevant evidence is sent immediately to teams to show them why.

Malyon adds: “One of the reasons I think we've been reasonably successful at completely removing track limits as a talking point is that we deployed the technology, shared the technology, and distributed the evidence freely to all the teams.”
But it is not just on regulatory matters where ROC has a role. It also supports race control on some safety matters, too.

One learning from George Russell’s penultimate lap crash in the 2024 Australian Grand Prix was that race control needed better information about the status of a car and driver once a crash has happened.
So now there is a bespoke desk that can help pull up all the relevant onboards and information to help race control work out what sort of intervention is needed.

Malyon added: “We realised at that time we needed a much quicker way to identify a car that had an issue, and provide all the information about that one car to be able to make an assessment of where it was - was it in a safe position? was it in an unsafe position? - and to allow us to progress as quickly as possible to a neutralisation if needed.”
The transformation of ROC since 2022 has been immense, as Malyon says where it is now is a world away from how it started. But equally, time was essential to actually understand what was needed.
“ROC 1.0 in its first inception was four people, sometimes one or two more,” he said. “Actually, as a facility, I was quite pleased at the time. It came together very quickly.
“We were able to repurpose a former race control desk - but it was ultimately a converted meeting room with a race control desk and a much smaller video wall.

“When we first started, obviously we had to understand the technology, but we also had to understand the relationships and the responsibilities, and it was something that grew quite organically. We were lucky enough to have a few key people in there that had experience of similar facilities that they'd used in teams or similar.
“As a result, I would say over the first six months there was a very, very significant ramp-up and a building of trust.

“I think that was key to the success, really, building that trust between race control and the ROC and understanding the right way to work together to be an effective force multiplier, not just another voice.
“And sometimes, as you'll know, a single voice making clear decisions is obviously very important when it comes to time pressure.”
Ultimately, technology can never replace humans when it comes to enforcing regulatory aspects – but what ROC intends to do is reduce the risk of mistakes being made.
As Ben Sulayem said: “Minimising the human error is very important - but getting rid of the human factor, it's impossible.”

Better information fuels better decisions, but ROC’s value comes also in making sure that race control and the race director can focus on critical areas and are not overwhelmed by having to do things that can be handled elsewhere.
The Abu Dhabi 2021 inquiry concluded that too much stress being placed on individuals’ shoulders only increased the danger of errors being made.
Had ROC 3.0 been around in 2021, then that year’s Abu Dhabi Grand Prix may not have turned into what it was.
But as Ben Sulayem says, time cannot be rolled back, and the important thing was that every effort was made to ensure the same mistakes were not repeated in the future.
“This promise was done,” he said. “What happened in Abu Dhabi in 2021 could have been avoided. But we can't go to the past. We have to go to the future.”

items.titleZh: 加斯利谈F1在美国的爆炸式增长：我假装自己是纳斯卡车手

items.originalTitle: 'I pretended to be a NASCAR driver' - Gasly on F1's US explosion
detailZh: 一级方程式在美国的飞速发展让车手们感受到了，阿尔皮纳的皮埃尔·加斯利指出，在过去十年中，这种对比非常明显。
在美国大奖赛前夕，加斯利在接受《赛车》CEO法布里西奥·德鲁蒙德采访时表示，F1在美国的增长‘实际上非常惊人’。
“我仍然记得2015年第一次来到美国时，人们会问我我在做什么，”他说。"我试图向他们解释我是一个一级方程式的预备车手。但几分钟后，我最终只能说我是那晚的纳斯卡车手。
“我只是……随便说说这个故事，因为当时人们对我们的运动还不太了解。而现在这实际上非常惊人。”
“你在奥斯汀市区转一圈，到处都是一级方程式的周边商品。我想整个周末将有五十万人来参加美国大奖赛。大多数赛道都挤满了人。”
“作为车手、作为车队、作为品牌，参与我们这项运动是令人难以置信的时刻。目前，我们正处于真正的势头之中。”
“我记得我小时候的Adobe”
加斯利讲述了他母亲Pascale 加斯利的另一个个人故事。皮埃尔与Adobe的Marissa Dacay一起发言，作为企业营销全球副总裁，她详细介绍了软件公司首次与阿尔派 F1车队的一级方程式合作。
“我记得小时候的Adobe；我妈妈经常做这种赞助宣传册，在我们家的电脑上，她经常熬夜寻找赞助商。”
"我还记得桌面上的Adobe品牌。那可能是我记得家里最早使用的软件之一。"
“所以，有他们加入我们真是太酷了。它显然是一个全球知名且非常高端的品牌。我相信，结合我们的力量，我们一定能取得非常成功的合作。”
Adobe将在2027赛季开始时与阿尔法罗密欧F1车队合作推出其软件并开始客户参与活动，生成式AI和Adobe的软件套件是合作的一部分。
“我认为我们有很多方法可以充分利用这次合作，”加斯利补充道。
“如今，在一级方程式赛车中，粉丝互动至关重要。在曝光度方面，我们看到越来越多的品牌在车队层面，甚至在车手层面都致力于一级方程式赛车——有更多的机会，更多的品牌，试图对我们团队，对我们表现，以及更广泛的视角，对粉丝产生积极影响。”
detailEn: Formula 1’s meteoric rise in the United States has been felt by the drivers, with Alpine’s Pierre Gasly having noted a stark contrast over the last decade.

Speaking to The Race CEO Fabricio Drumond at 'Formula One's Premium Playbook', an event hosted by The Race and Axios ahead of the US Grand Prix, Gasly said that F1’s growth in the United States is “actually amazing”.

“I still remember coming to the States back in 2015 and people would ask me what I was doing," he said. "And I tried to explain to them I'm a reserve F1 driver. And after a couple minutes, I just ended up saying I'm a NASCAR driver for the night.
“I was just…going with that story, because people didn't yet have the knowledge about our sport. And now it's actually amazing.

“You go around town [in Austin], everybody's wearing Formula 1 merch. I think half a million people are going to show up across the weekend [at the US GP]. Most of the racetracks are absolutely packed.
“It's an amazing time to be part of our sport as a driver, as a team, as a brand. There is a real momentum at the moment.”
'I remember Adobe from when I was a kid'

Gasly recounted another personal anecdote about his mother, Pascale Gasly. Pierre spoke alongside Adobe’s Marissa Dacay, as the global VP of enterprise marketing detailed the software company’s first entry into F1 partnerships with the Alpine F1 team.
“I remember Adobe from when I was a kid; my mum used to do this sponsoring brochure, and on the computer we had she was spending nights and nights trying to look for sponsors.
"And I remember the Adobe branding on the desktop. It was probably one of the first sorts of softwares I remember my family using.

“So it's definitely very cool to have them on board with us. It's obviously a worldwide known and very premium brand. And I'm sure combining our forces, we're definitely going to make it a very successful collaboration.”

Adobe will roll out its software and begin customer engagement campaigns in partnership with the Alpine F1 team at the start of the 2027 F1 season, with generative AI and Adobe’s software suite part of the deal.
“I think there's many ways that we're going to be able to make the best out of this partnership," Gasly added.

"Nowadays, fan engagement is critical in Formula 1. In terms of exposure, we can see a lot more brands are committing to Formula 1 on a team level, but also on a driver level - a lot more opportunities, a lot more brands and trying to have a positive impact for our team, for our performance, but also bigger picture, for the fans."
keyPointsZh: 加斯利在采访中提到F1在美国的受欢迎程度有所提升。
加斯利认为现在是成为F1运动中的一部分的绝佳时机。
keyPointsEn: Pierre Gasly mentioned the increased popularity of Formula 1 in the United States.
Gasly believes it's an excellent time to be part of Formula 1 as a driver, team, or brand.

detailZh: 乔治·拉塞尔：2026赛季是‘性格和韧性’的考验
随着他成为冠军的希望似乎化为泡影，乔治·拉塞尔解释了他为何认为2026年的‘艰难’课程不会对他的发展造成损害
乔治·拉塞尔认为，2026赛季的F1对他意志的考验几乎让他所有的冠军希望都破灭了，但他感觉这一年来的自我反省让他对如何驾驶当前车型有了突破
尽管拉塞尔以胜利开始了这一年，作为梅赛德斯车队以最快的赛车开始赛季，他被标记为早期冠军的有力竞争者，但他的队友基米·安东内利并不需要很长时间就能在他的资深队友身上找到优势，并凭借强劲的早期势头建立起自己的冠军领先优势。
安东内利的成功和拉塞尔今年上半年的表现下滑，让车队英国一侧的人们感到困惑。拉塞尔将他的积分差距部分归因于运气不佳，但也承认自己的表现并未达到预期。
在寻求结果的过程中，拉塞尔觉得自己现在已经理解了2026年车型的要求。他的理论是，安东内利在后期应用油门踏板，以及专注于弯道的早期阶段——与拉塞尔自然倾向于攻击弯道的中后段并提前调校动力——更容易与2026年车型产生共鸣。
“就我本赛季的心态和对锦标赛的看法来说，我认为它是起伏不定的。在年初我积分差距很大的时候，让我夜不能寐的事情是我的表现不足，”拉塞尔说。
“我在想，‘我该如何提高我的表现？我从汽车那里需要什么？汽车需要我从驾驶中获取什么？’，而不是我的机会可能错失。”
“我从70分落后到银石站后的25分，然后差距又扩大了，然后，你知道的，巴库发生了。这让我再次的机会感觉很大。然后，当然，一周后，它又下降了，新加坡的网格处罚让伤口更加痛苦。”
“这个赛季本来就不应该这样。但我对它并不怨恨。我会回顾我本可以做得更好和应该做得更好的领域，而不是那些我无法控制且对我不利的事情。”
““我认为，在运气不好的方面，和我表现不佳的方面一样多，我知道我能够做到的极限。所以，是的，这就是现实。”"
“拉塞尔表示，在赛季开始之前，他已经确信如何应对锦标赛，因为他年轻时通过一场又一场的比赛方法赢得了GP3和二级方程式冠军，而追求整体性能的提升正是这一点。”"
他说，关于这一点，锦标赛的竞争并没有给他带来任何新的东西，但他觉得在2026年所面临的困难最终会使他成为一个更强的车手。
"在我的青训车队时期，我为了锦标赛而战斗过，我知道我想要如何去应对，那就是一场比赛一场比赛地来。"
"但是，正如我今年早些时候说的那样，当表现不在那里时，我没有考虑锦标赛。我唯一关注的是表现。"
"今年对我来说是一次真正的性格和韧性的考验，通过艰难的比赛、不幸的事件，以及不得不照镜子审视自己，思考如何从这些时刻中反弹回来？我是想要为此哭泣并让它对我产生负面影响，还是想要反弹回来并战斗以纠正它？"
“我认为这将会帮助我在接下来的10-15年职业生涯中成为一个更好的人和更好的车手。”
detailEn: George Russell: F1 2026 season a test of "character and resilience"
As his bid to be champion looks to come to nought, George Russell explained why his "tough" 2026 lessons won't be to his detriment

George Russell feels that the 2026 Formula 1 season has been a test of his resolve as his championship hopes have all but slipped away, but feels his soul-searching across the year has led him to a breakthrough in how to drive with the current cars.

Although Russell opened the year with victory, having been marked as the early championship favourite as Mercedes started the season with the fastest car, his team-mate Kimi Antonelli did not need long to find an advantage over his more senior team-mate and build his championship lead with strong early momentum.

Antonelli's successes and Russell's dwindling performances over the first half of the year led to much head-scratching on the Briton's side of the garage. Russell partly attributes his points deficit to bad luck, but also conceded that his performances were not up to scratch.

In his search for results, Russell feels he now understands the demands of the 2026 cars. His theory is that Antonelli's later application of the throttle pedal, and focus on the early phase of the corners – as opposed to Russell's natural stance to attack the mid-to-late section and dial in the power early – has chimed more easily with the 2026 cars.

"In terms of my mentality this season and my view of the championship as being up and down, early in the year when I had a big points deficit, the thing that was keeping me up at night was my lack of performance," Russell said.
"[I was] thinking like, 'How am I going to improve my performance? What do I need from the car? What does the car need from my driving?', rather than my opportunity maybe going amiss.

"I came from 70 points down to within 25 points post-Silverstone and then the gap extended and then, you know, Baku happened. That felt pretty big in terms of my chances again. And then, of course, one week later, it sort of kicked down again, and salt added to the wound with the grid penalty in Singapore.

"This season just hasn't meant to be. But I'm not bitter about it. I'll look back on the areas I could have done better and should have done better as opposed to things that have been out of my control that have gone against me.

"And I'd say as much has gone against me in terms of bad luck, there's been as much of my performances that haven't been to the scratch that I know I'm capable of. So, yeah, that's the reality of it."

Russell says that he was already sure of how to tackle the championship ahead of the season, having pursued the race-by-race approach that carried him to GP3 and Formula 2 titles in his younger years, and that the quest for improved performance overall played into that.
He says the championship battle hasn't unveiled anything new to him in that regard, but feels the difficulties faced over 2026 will make him a stronger driver in the long run.
"I fought for championships in my junior days, I knew how I wanted to approach it, and that was more by a race-by-race basis," he added.
"But, as I said earlier in the year when the performance wasn't there, I wasn't thinking about the championship. I was solely focused on the performance.

"This year has been a real test of my character and resilience through the tough races, the misfortune, and having to look at myself in the mirror and think, how do I want to bounce back from these moments? Do I want to cry about it and let it impact me negatively, or do I want to bounce back and fight and rectify it?
"And I think that's going to help me be a better person and better driver over the course of the next 10-15 years of my career."

items.titleZh: Adobe与阿尔派达成首个F1合作
items.summaryZh: 美国软件巨头Adobe在2026年美国大奖赛前宣布与阿尔派车队达成其首个F1合作，重点围绕车迷互动展开。Adobe高管Marissa Dacay表示，F1是最具数据驱动和性能驱动的运动，与Adobe高度契合。

media.altZh: Adobe与阿尔派达成首个F1合作 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: Why F1 is 'an incredible match’ for Adobe
items.summaryEn: US software giant Adobe announced its first F1 partnership with the Alpine team ahead of the 2026 United States Grand Prix, centred on fan engagement. Adobe global VP of enterprise marketing Marissa Dacay said F1 is the most data-driven and performance-driven sport, making it an incredible match for the company.
detailZh: 美国软件巨头Adobe在2026年美国大奖赛前宣布了其首个F1合作，称F1对Adobe而言是“绝佳的匹配”。
在奥斯汀由The Race与Axios共同举办的活动“Formula One's Premium Playbook”上，Adobe全球企业营销副总裁Marissa Dacay接受The Race首席执行官Fabricio Drumond采访时，解释了公司为何希望通过与阿尔派的新协议参与F1。
“没有哪项运动比F1更数据驱动、更性能驱动，”她说，“所以这对我们来说是绝佳的匹配，因为我们同样依靠数据、性能和创造力运转。”
“眼下也是运用技术的绝佳时机，想想F1，24场比赛、多种语言：大量的文化与细微差异。”
“在每个比赛周末、贯穿全年、以规模化方式、通过你们与车迷沟通的每一个渠道，你们要如何以个性化和具有文化细腻度的方式，去触达并对话你们的车迷？”
此次合作以推动车迷互动为核心，这家软件公司将为 阿尔派 部署其人工智能解决方案，以吸引受众与 阿尔派 互动。
Adobe GenStudio 将使 阿尔派 能够管理和策划面向全球车迷的营销活动，同时这支 F1 车队还将部署 Experience Platform 和 Brand Visibility。
与此同时，车迷将有机会在 阿尔派 未来开展的互动活动中使用 Adobe Express。
达卡伊表示，Adobe 与恩斯通F1车队有着“共同的愿景”。
“这对我们来说是一个全新的篇章。这是一项真正全球性的运动，这对我们非常重要。体育是连接技术、人文、创造力和文化的绝佳方式。
“因此，当我们寻找合作伙伴时，关键在于——我们如何拥有共同的愿景，即如何将这项运动或车队的表现、技术、创造力和人工智能融为一体，从而改变车迷与车队或这项运动互动的方式。
“此外，现在还有一个机会——车迷不再只是消费我们推送到他们面前的内容。他们希望参与到创作讲述故事的内容中来。
“他们想成为故事的主角。我认为，没有比我们自己的工具更好的工具，能帮助车迷参与车队活动，更近距离地感受到自己真正是这项运动中车队的一部分。”
达凯补充说，Adobe 的全套产品已经部署在大型体育营销活动中，而且其使用方式很多人并不了解。
“大家可能已经因为 PDF、Photoshop，以及 Adobe 四十多年来所做的所有事情而认识我们，”她说。
“没有多少人知道我们从事的是营销和客户体验编排业务。所以，当你使用车队应用、收到电子邮件，或者看到扑面而来的营销内容时，你所获得的许多个性化体验，很多都是由 Adobe 提供支持的。”
“因此，我们这里的机会在于超越人们所熟知的 Adobe 的创造力和文档类传统业务，并开始建立这样一种联系：当你与像 阿尔派 这样的品牌或像 阿尔派 这样的车队互动时，作为一名车迷你获得了绝佳的体验，而我们正是背后的支撑，让他们能够理解你和你的偏好。
“我们正是背后为你量身定制那一刻内容的力量。我们正是背后让你无论身处何地都能触达你的力量，无论是在手机上、电视上、应用上，还是在流媒体上。
“这正是我们希望在与体育的这些连接中去解锁的东西。”
detailEn: Formula 1 is an "incredible match" for US software giant Adobe, which announced its first F1 partnership in the lead-up to the 2026 United States Grand Prix.

Speaking to The Race CEO Fabricio Drumond at 'Formula One's Premium Playbook', an event hosted by The Race and Axios in Austin, Adobe’s global VP of enterprise marketing Marissa Dacay explained why the company wanted to get involved in F1 through its new deal with Alpine.

“There's no sport that's more data-driven, more performance-driven than Formula 1,” she said. “So it's just an incredible match for us, because we live through data and performance and creativity as well.
"Right now, it's an incredible time to use tech, too, if you think about F1, 24 races, multiple languages: tonnes of culture and nuance.

“How do you scale the way you're going to reach and speak to your fans in a personalised and culturally nuanced way, every weekend throughout the entire year, at scale, across every channel that you're speaking to your fans?”
The partnership is centred around driving fan engagement, with the software company to deploy its AI solutions to engage audiences with Alpine.
Adobe GenStudio will enable Alpine to manage and curate its marketing campaigns for fans around the world, with Experience Platform and Brand Visibility also set to be deployed by the F1 team.
Meanwhile, fans will be given the opportunity to use Adobe Express in forthcoming activations involving Alpine.
Dacay said Adobe has a “shared vision” with the Enstone F1 team.
“This one is a brand new chapter for us. It's a truly global sport, which is really important to us. Sports are such an amazing way to connect technology, humanity, creativity, culture.

“And so, when we're looking for a partner, it's - how do we have this shared vision about how we're bringing the performance of the sport or the team, technology, creativity, AI all together to change the way fans are going to engage with the team or with the sport.
“Also, there's an opportunity now - fans aren't just consuming the content that we're pushing out in front of them. They want to be part of creating the content that tells the story.

“They want to be the story. I think there's no better tools out there than our own to help fans participate with the team and get closer to actually feeling like they're part of the team in the sport.”
Dacay added that Adobe’s suite is already deployed in major sports marketing campaigns, and that it is used in ways that many people are unaware of.
“You all probably already know us for PDF, for Photoshop, for all the things that Adobe has done for over 40 years," she said.

“Not a lot of folks know that we're in the marketing, customer experience orchestration business. So a lot of the personalised experiences that you get when you're engaging with an app for the team, or you're receiving an email, or you're seeing marketing just out hitting you, a lot of that is powered by Adobe.

“So the opportunity we have here is to go beyond the creativity and document kind of heritage that you know Adobe for, and start to build the connection that when you engage with a brand like Alpine or a team like Alpine, and you have an incredible experience as a fan, we're behind why they understand you and your preferences.
"We're behind the content that was customised for you in that moment. We're behind reaching you wherever you are, whether it's on the phone, on TV, on an app, on streaming.
"That's the thing that we're looking to unlock in these connections with sports.”

keyPointsEn: Adobe will deploy Adobe GenStudio, Experience Platform and Brand Visibility with Alpine to manage and curate marketing campaigns for fans worldwide.
Fans will be given the opportunity to use Adobe Express in forthcoming activations involving Alpine.
Dacay cited F1's 24 races and multiple languages as bringing tonnes of culture and nuance, requiring a personalised way to reach fans.
